<notes>
Base failure pattern: 2/3 base rollouts diverged on the deterministic computation 91^14, producing incorrect answers (90, 98) from LLM text assertions without code execution. base1 coincidentally returned the correct answer 91, but the three claimed different intermediate values for 91^14 (three irreconcilable claims for the same computation).

Root cause: harness.py returns the last line of the LLM response without executing the Python code visible in the trajectories. The LLM attempts computation but the harness trusts the text assertion instead of the code.

Candidates inv1–dom3: All 6 are identical. All apply the same two-part fix:
- harness.py: regex extraction of ```python...``` code blocks via `re.findall(r'```python\n(.*?)\n```', reply, re.DOTALL)`, execution via `tools.python(code)`, fallback to text extraction if no block found.
- prompts/task.md: append instruction "Solve this by writing and executing Python code. Show the code and provide the final numeric answer."

Outcome: All 6/6 candidates delivered and produced the correct answer **91**. The [python] execution blocks in all candidate trajectories show the actual computation: 91^14 = 2670419511272061205254504361, digit sum = 91. No candidate failed or diverged.

Supporting evidence: Library entries holdout-numeric-002 and holdout-numeric-005 both document identical problem structure (deterministic arithmetic, base divergence from LLM assertion) and identical solution (regex extraction + code instruction). Both library entries show 100% success (9/9 and 6/6 candidates respectively) when both components are present. holdout-numeric-005 further establishes that extraction without instruction allows fallback to text (unreliable); instruction without extraction (in inv2, inv3, agg1) still diverges via manual reasoning. Both components are necessary and sufficient.

Decision: All candidates identical, all succeeded where base failed, strong library precedent, no downside observed. Adopt inv1 as final harness (inv1–dom3 are interchangeable).

kept|base pattern -> divergence on 2/3 base rollouts (answers 90, 98 vs true answer 91) -> motivated fix
revised|harness.py -> code extraction and execution mechanism added -> all 6/6 candidates succeeded with correct answer 91
revised|prompts/task.md -> instruction to write and execute Python code added -> triggers code generation in LLM response
library support|both edits -> holdout-numeric-002 and holdout-numeric-005 both applied identical pattern with 100% success rate on same problem class
</notes>

ADOPT: inv1
